title: Dedicated staged rollouts (reserved pools) — MVP scope working notes
content:
Doc purpose (working notes): align Console + Dedicated MVP for staged rollouts on reserved pools. This is intentionally rough; PRD/spec will be the source of truth.

Last updated: 2025-03-06 (post beta check-in prep)
Owner: Marissa (Console & Rollouts) | Co-owner: Lauren (Dedicated)

---

1) Problem statement (why now)
- Dedicated customers have asked for safer upgrades to pool model/runtime/config without downtime and without “all-or-nothing” risk.
- Current situation: we can roll changes, but Dedicated routing/partitioning + limited guardrails means early canaries can cause unexpected capacity starvation (429s) and it’s hard to prove safety / show evidence.
- We need an operator/customer-admin friendly staged rollout plan with explicit stages + objective gates + abort/rollback with audit.

Customer signal snippets (paraphrased from Support/Sales)
- SUP-28491 (Dedicated customer escalation): “We need to upgrade model versions, but we can’t take an outage and we can’t accept surprises. We need a canary stage with clear stop/go based on error/latency and capacity.”
- Sales deep dive 2025-02-06 (Dedicated prospect): “We have change management. If you can’t show audit logs of who promoted and why, we can’t use it for production.”
- Beta-ish feedback theme: “We want staged rollout, but the stage needs to preserve effective capacity; a 1% split can still mean 50% of the GPUs if the partitioning is wrong.”

Non-customer but crucial internal: SRE concerns about missing metrics / telemetry lag leading to false ‘pass’ decisions. Preference: fail-closed with explicit override + audit.

---

2) What exactly is “Dedicated staged rollout” in v1
Definition (for MVP):
- A rollout plan attached to a Dedicated pool (or pool+region) that moves a target change from stable → canary → partial → full using stages.
- Each stage has:
  - A traffic allocation (percentage OR replica partition) to “candidate” vs “stable”
  - Gate checks (latency/errors/saturation/health) evaluated on stage-specific metrics
  - Promotion action (manual at first; automated evaluation in MVP-v1.5 depending on timeline)
  - Abort/rollback action
  - Hold state (freeze where nothing changes)

Supported change types (MVP):
- Model version update (e.g., model artifact + tokenizer)
- Runtime build update (serving engine build)
- Routing policy config update (e.g., caching/batching toggles, max_tokens defaults, quant profile)
- NOTE: not promising “arbitrary experimentation platform” beyond rollout safety.

---

3) MVP goals (what we must ship)
Console UX goals
- A dedicated “Rollout plan” view for a Dedicated pool:
  - Timeline of stages (Draft → Running stage N → Completed/Aborted/Held)
  - Clear gate status per stage: Pass / Fail / Unknown (missing data) / Not evaluated
  - Action buttons: Promote, Abort, Hold, Resume (depending on state and RBAC)
  - Evidence drawer: show gate query window, observed value, threshold, pass/fail reason
  - Change history / audit trail: who did what, when, with reason strings

Platform/control plane goals
- CRUD for Dedicated rollout plans + stage list
- Deterministic state machine for stage promotion/abort/hold
- Idempotent promote/abort actions (retry-safe)
- Audit event emission on all actions incl overrides

Routing/data plane goals
- Ability to split requests across stable vs candidate capacity for a Dedicated pool.
- Must avoid canary partition starving stable traffic or vice versa.
- Multi-region behavior must be explicit (see open questions).

Observability goals
- Stage-tagged metrics/traces for key signals
- Standard “gate templates” (Redwood-defined metrics; limited config)
- Default dashboards for operators + SRE
- Promotion/abort annotations on dashboards

---

4) MVP scope boundaries (explicit non-goals for initial release)
- No arbitrary customer-defined custom metrics for gating (only Redwood-defined signals + limited thresholds / windows config)
- No multi-armed bandit / generalized A/B experimentation UI
- No “per-endpoint” or “per-model-route” staged rollouts inside the same Dedicated pool beyond the designated candidate/stable split for the rollout target
- No promise that every workload gets quality regression gates in MVP (we may support “optional quality gate” if eval harness is ready + customer has prompt sets)

---

5) Proposed default stages (current proposal)
Default stage set (subject to infra guardrails / small pool constraints):
- Stage 0: 0% candidate (baseline; mostly for setup/validation)
- Stage 1 (canary): 1% candidate
- Stage 2: 10% candidate
- Stage 3: 50% candidate
- Stage 4: 100% candidate

Notes
- For Dedicated pools we may need replica-based partitions rather than pure percentage (esp. small pools). Example: 1 GPU canary, rest stable.
- Naming in UI: “Canary (1%)”, “Ramp (10%)”, “Half (50%)”, “Full (100%)”
- UX needs to communicate whether “%” is traffic-weight or capacity partition. We should avoid implying precision we can’t deliver.

Small pool exception idea (needs infra sign-off)
- If pool size < N GPUs (N TBD, likely 8 or 16), stage set should switch to replica counts:
  - 0/1/2/… GPU candidate
- Console should show “1 GPU” rather than “1%”.

---

6) Gate signals (MVP) — what we check before promote
Minimum required gates (proposal)
- Error rate gate (5xx and/or Redwood error classes)
- Latency gate (p95 and maybe p99 for select tiers)
- Saturation/headroom gate (GPU util, queue depth, or “time in queue”)
- OOM / crash loop gate (OOM rate, pod restarts)
- Request drop / throttling gate (429 rate)
- GPU/node health gate (ECC errors / node taints / throttling) (might be “advisory” in v1 depending on data availability)

Nice-to-have gates (likely v2)
- Quality regression (eval harness) — only if customer has prompt sets + we can run reliably; otherwise risk of blocking promotions forever.
- Cost regression (tokens/sec vs cost) — more of a post-stage report than a hard gate.

Gate evaluation principles (consensus so far)
- Must be objective, time-windowed, and based on stage-tagged metrics.
- Must handle missing/lagging telemetry.
- Must be auditable: record which signals were used + observed values at decision time.

Open: exact default thresholds (see PM-827). SRE wants alignment with SLO + error budget.

---

7) Manual vs automated gates (phasing)
Phase split (rough)
- MVP “beta”: gates evaluated automatically but promotion remains manual (operator clicks Promote), with UI showing Pass/Fail/Unknown.
- Auto-abort: likely on by default for “hard fail” thresholds (e.g., huge 5xx spike) after a short confirmation window (TBD). Need to be careful with false positives.
- Fully automated “promote when gates pass for X minutes” not in initial beta unless we’re confident in signal reliability.

Reason: automation + noisy metrics + small sample sizes can create churn.

---

8) Console UX requirements (working notes)
Core screens
- Dedicated Pool → Rollouts tab
  - Current rollout plan (if any): summary state + stage + candidate target
  - Create plan (if none) with default stages + default gates (editable within constraints)
- Rollout Plan detail
  - Stage timeline component
  - Gate status matrix: stage x gate (or per-stage expandable)
  - Evidence drawer
  - Action bar: Promote / Abort / Hold / Resume
  - “Overrides” area: Force promote, Force abort (admin only), with red warning copy + required reason text
  - Audit trail section (filterable, export link maybe later)

UX notes from early reviews
- Hold needs to be explicit (“freeze traffic split and stop evaluation” vs “stop promotion only”). We likely need two concepts but MVP should choose one.
- Gate “Unknown” due to missing metrics needs clear messaging:
  - “Telemetry delayed (last datapoint 7m ago). Gate evaluation paused. You can hold, wait, or force promote (admin).”

---

9) RBAC + audit (must-have)
Roles (proposal)
- Customer Admin: can create rollout plan, promote, abort, hold (within their account)
- Customer Viewer: read-only
- Redwood Operator (internal): same + ability to troubleshoot across accounts
- Redwood Admin / SRE: can force-promote/force-abort, bypass gates, edit locked fields (guardrails)

Audit events (minimum)
- dedicated_pool_rollout.created
- dedicated_pool_rollout.updated
- dedicated_pool_rollout.promoted
- dedicated_pool_rollout.aborted
- dedicated_pool_rollout.held
- dedicated_pool_rollout.resumed
- dedicated_pool_rollout.force_promoted (explicit override flag)
- dedicated_pool_rollout.force_aborted

Audit event fields (must capture)
- actor_id, actor_type (user/service), account_id, pool_id, region(s)
- from_stage → to_stage
- reason (required for overrides; optional for normal)
- gate_snapshot_id or embedded summary (observed values + thresholds)

---

10) Key technical constraints (what can break)
Capacity fragmentation risk
- Partitioning the pool can reduce effective throughput if partitions can’t borrow capacity.
- Canary stage is the worst offender: a small candidate partition may get overloaded quickly and produce 429s, or stable gets starved if routing is not careful.
- We need explicit guardrails: min headroom, min replica counts, and queue depth protections.

Telemetry cardinality risk
- Stage tags add label cardinality. Need allowlist and strict tag set. (We already saw a regression in a prior attempt; be conservative.)

Streaming behavior
- Rollback during streaming: do we pin in-flight streams to the backend that started them? Likely yes.
- Rollback semantics should avoid cutting streams mid-response.

Multi-region Dedicated
- If pool spans regions, stage allocation must be well-defined:
  - Option A: stage applies per-region (each region has candidate/stable split)
  - Option B: stage applies globally (routing shifts across regions)
- Need to avoid a partial region impairment causing “global fail” without context.

---

11) Open questions (need decisions)
Stage representation
1) Percent-based vs replica-based stages: do we support both in MVP, or pick one and map behind the scenes?
   - My take: UI can show percent; backend should support replica constraints and display effective partition.
2) Default stage set: 1/10/50/100 vs 1/5/25/50/100 vs customizable stages.
   - Concern: too many knobs in Console for v1.

Gate evaluation behavior under missing data
3) Fail-open vs fail-closed when telemetry is stale:
   - SRE position: fail-closed (promotion blocked) + manual override (admin) with audit.
   - PM concern: customers will get stuck if telemetry pipeline hiccups.
   - Proposal: fail-closed after staleness threshold (e.g., 3-5 mins) and show “Unknown”; allow Hold; allow force promote with reason + admin.

Minimum sample size
4) Do we require a minimum request count/token count before evaluating latency/error gates?
   - Without min sample, low-traffic canary may look “perfect” but meaningless.
   - Need a default: e.g., at least 200 requests OR 1M tokens in window (numbers TBD).

Auto-abort rules
5) Should we auto-abort on “severe” failures (e.g., 5xx > X%) even if customer wants to inspect first?
   - If auto-abort exists, must be clearly visible and configurable (maybe on/off per plan, admin only).

Multi-region policy
6) If one region fails a gate and another passes, do we block promotion globally?
   - MVP proposal: block global promotion; present per-region evidence; allow operator to exclude impaired region (likely v2).

Customer visibility of overrides
7) When Redwood staff force-promotes/overrides, do customer admins see it?
   - Should be yes (audit), but may need a distinction: “Redwood operator action” vs “customer action.”

What is “Hold” exactly
8) Hold semantics:
   - Hold traffic split constant + stop evaluation? OR hold only blocks stage transitions while evaluation continues?
   - MVP preference: hold freezes split AND blocks transitions; gate evaluation continues but does not trigger anything.

Quality gate (optional)
9) Do we include a placeholder UI for “quality gates” even if not broadly supported?
   - Risk: we over-promise. If included, must be clearly labeled “optional / requires eval setup.”

---

12) MVP acceptance criteria (rough)
- Operator can create a rollout plan with default stages + gates for a Dedicated pool.
- Candidate traffic can be shifted by stage without causing catastrophic capacity starvation under typical loads.
- Console displays per-stage gate status + evidence with correct stage attribution.
- Promote/abort/hold are idempotent and audited.
- Missing metrics blocks promotion by default and is clearly messaged.
- Runbook exists for oncall when a gate fails.

---

13) Next steps / TODO (as of last edit)
- [Paula] finalize default gate thresholds proposal (PM-827) w/ SRE sign-off.
- [Lauren + Irene/Vanessa] confirm min pool size + partitioning guardrails; decide replica-based fallback behavior for small pools.
- [Marissa + Kenji] stage timeline component: confirm states + copy for Unknown/Hold/Override.
- [Logan] confirm stage tag set and cardinality limits; document staleness detection.
- [Ethan + Mina] confirm multi-region semantics for stage application.
- [Rafael/Sean] draft “no promote during incident / high error budget burn” rule (even if manual gate in v1).
